shifts.summary: Candidates reported the shift as overall Easy to Moderate. Reasoning was generally easy with many statement‑based and blood‑relation items. General Awareness difficulty varied widely, while Mathematics was seen as moderate with many mensuration questions. English was mostly easy but passages were long and time‑tight.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates found reasoning easy or simple, with many statement‑based and blood‑relation items. Some described it as moderate but overall manageable.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS varied; some found it as expected with statistics, others reported difficulty and out‑of‑syllabus items, while some said it was okay and static.

topics.topic: General Awareness (GS) similar to previous years

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math was the toughest part with many mensuration questions; some reported it as manageable with formula‑based practice, while others found it difficult and time‑tight.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was comfortable with previous‑year passages, though some found the passage long and time‑tight. Vocabulary and para‑jumbles were prominent.

intro: The SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted on 9 October 2026 across three shifts. Shift 1 has been reported as Easy to Moderate overall, with good attempts ranging between 75 and 98. Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending analysis and will be updated after the shifts conclude. All figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 on 9 October 2026 was reported as Easy to Moderate, while the difficulty for Shifts 2 and 3 is not yet available and will be added after their analysis.

faqs.q: How many attempts were considered good for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: For Shift 1 on 9 October 2026, good attempts were reported to be between 75 and 98. No data is currently available for Shifts 2 and 3.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for Shifts 2 and 3 of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026 be posted?
faqs.a: The analysis for Shifts 2 and 3 will be added a few hours after each shift ends, once sufficient candidate reviews are collected.

faqs.q: Are the figures reported for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No, the figures are unofficial and based on candidate feedback; SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: Does SSC normalise scores across different shifts for the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, SSC applies a normalisation process to ensure scores are comparable across all shifts of the exam.
